title: Word 24 — On Love
attribution_note: Word 24 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Malice kills; love brings to life. Dead is he who lives in malice, and alive is he who abides in love.
Malice works evil; love works no evil, but works good.
Malice is the devil's seed; love is God's seed.
The former are like apples beautiful on the outside but bitter and worm-eaten within; the latter are like apples unattractive on the outside but sweet and delicious within.
But let us look at the fruits of love, that as a tree is known by its fruit, so we may know love by its works. For love is known by its deeds, not by its words.

sections.heading: What love would banish, if it truly reigned

pairs.en: Beloved Christians! If we possessed true love, it would take from us every misfortune and bring in every blessing: our cities, towns, villages, and homes would become a place of paradise, filled with joy and sweetness. For love cannot exist without this. If love were in people, we would not fear robbery, murder, violence, and plunder, for *“love does no wrong to a neighbor”* [Romans 13:10]. If love existed, there would be no theft, stealing, or other evil, because *“love does no wrong to a neighbor.”* If love existed, people would not touch their neighbor's marriage bed, because *“love does no wrong to a neighbor.”* If love existed, people would not suffer slander, reproach, insult, mockery, dishonor, and other evils, for *“love does no wrong to a neighbor.”* If love existed, people would not deceive us, nor delude us, nor lie to us: *“love does no wrong to a neighbor.”*

If love existed, rulers would not complain of their subjects nor subjects of their rulers, because rulers would build up society and subjects would obey them. For the same reason, shepherds would not complain of their flocks nor flocks of their shepherds, masters would not complain of servants and peasants nor servants and peasants of masters, parents would not complain of children nor children of parents, and so on.

Today Christians love to live in rich houses, to sit at rich tables, to dress in rich clothing, to ride in fine carriages and on fine horses, even while seeing the want and poverty of their neighbors. From this it is evident that they love only themselves, and not God and their neighbors. This is why every misfortune, calamity, and wretchedness comes upon people. For the cause of all evil is self-love. Therefore the Lover of mankind, caring for our well-being, gave us this commandment: *“love your neighbor as yourself”* [Matthew 22:39].

sections.heading: The present coldness, and the call to love

pairs.en: Christians, woe to us without love! Where there is no love, there is no faith, for faith cannot exist without love; and where there is no faith, there is no Christ and no salvation. Christians! We confess a God who is Love [1 John 4:8]. *“Let us love one another, that with one mind we may confess the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.”* Amen.
